description: The High Resolution Channel of Hubble’s Advanced Camera for Surveys provided high spatial resolution imaging from near-ultraviolet to near-infrared wavelengths. Its archived modes include imaging filters, polarimetry, a grism and a prism; the channel has been unavailable since January 2007.
facility_description: The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope is a 2.4-m reflecting telescope operating in low-Earth orbit.
notes: Researched 2026-10-26. Licence classification applies to STScI-produced, unmarked calibration data under the STScI content use policy, which separately requests NASA/STScI acknowledgement. Separately copyrighted third-party material is excluded. Do not redistribute the cited papers themselves under this data policy. Original source family is STScI synphot component tables; the owner throughput documentation explains total-system response. Existing NJM curves were not downloaded, hash-matched, replaced or assigned a new calibration epoch in this research. No DetectorType changes. The HST acknowledgement is copied verbatim as a conditional publication template, including its unfilled program placeholder. No grant acknowledgement is claimed. Sirianni et al. (2005) characterises the fixed imaging-filter response curves; Bohlin (2016) updates the CCD photometric calibration. Ramp filters, polarizers, prisms and grisms are deliberately not given that imaging-paper reference. The owner ACS throughput page describes photon detection efficiency and date-dependent response; its plotted WFC/SBC reference epoch is MJD 60035 and HRC MJD 54136, which must not be assumed to be the epoch of existing NJM curves.
